target.title: fix(browser): time out response body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Browser response body capture could hang past its timeout when Playwright matched the response headers but the response body read never completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The response-body path now carries the existing response deadline through the Playwright `response.body()` read instead of clearing the timer after the matching response event. This keeps the existing URL matching and body truncation behavior while preventing a stalled body read from holding the tool call indefinitely.

## User Impact

Users and automation that wait for a Browser response body now get a bounded timeout failure instead of a stuck command when the response body never resolves.

## Evidence

Current head: `536594b9ddc892528c2b3a15466a78a0af7a217a`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.responses.e2e.test.ts` passed on the PR head: 1 real Chromium test proving a matched response body read times out after the deadline.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.responses.test.ts` passed on the PR head: 2 unit tests covering the timeout and normal matched-body cases.

target.title: fix(browser): cap fields-file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser CLI action commands accept `--fields-file` for form field descriptors. The previous reader loaded the whole file into memory before validating or parsing it, so a very large fields file could be fully buffered before the CLI rejected it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow 1 MiB byte cap to the `--fields-file` path only. The reader consumes at most the cap plus one sentinel byte, rejects oversized files before JSON parsing, documents the limit in Browser CLI help and docs, and leaves inline `--fields` behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Users get a friendly size-limit error for oversized Browser CLI fields files instead of the CLI buffering arbitrarily large input. Existing valid fields files up to the documented 1 MiB limit and inline JSON fields continue to work.

## Evidence

Current head: `e029080cbc7f9ff23196914e772a6959a739b480`.

- Real behavior proof: `node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs --input-type=module <inline proof script>` imported `readFields` from the current head and exercised valid, exact-limit, and oversized `--fields-file` inputs while confirming the Browser CLI docs mention the 1 MiB contract. Final terminal output:

```json
{
  "head": "e029080cbc7f9ff23196914e772a6959a739b480",
  "maxBytes": 1048576,
  "validFieldsFile": [
    {
      "ref": "proof-ref",
      "type": "text",
      "value": "from file"
    }
  ],
  "exactLimitFieldsFile": {
    "bytes": 1048576,
    "ref": "exact-ref",
    "valueLength": 1048544
  },
  "oversizedFieldsFile": {
    "accepted": false,
    "error": "fields file exceeds 1048576 bytes"
  },
  "docsMentionLimit": true
}
```

- Focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.test.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.form-wait-eval.test.ts` passed 2 files / 19 tests.
- Formatting and whitespace: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check docs/cli/browser.md extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.form-wait-eval.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.test.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.ts` passed; `git diff --check origin/qingminlong/browser-fields-file-cap-v2~1...HEAD -- docs/cli/browser.md extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.form-wait-eval.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.test.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.ts` passed.
